convention: FKL arXiv 1212.4545v1 p.4 Sec. 3.3 and FKLR arXiv 2303.00079v2 p.7 eq. (3.1): (lambda1, lambda2) with lambda1 >= lambda2 >= 0, lambda3 = -lambda1 - lambda2; spectral (Langlands) parameters mu_j = i*lambda_j in Gamma_R(s + mu_j). One point per pair {F, dual F}; the dual has conj(a_p) and parameters -lambda_j (FKL p.4; FKLR p.4 "the bar indicates Schwarz reflection ... is the dual of L"; p.7). Laplace eigenvalue = 1 + lambda1^2 + lambda1*lambda2 + lambda2^2 (FKLR eq. (6.5) p.19: 1 + (l1^2+l2^2+l3^2)/2; Miller Duke p.25 eq. (10) context: lambda = (n^3-n)/24 - sum mu_j^2/2). a_p = A(p,1) in analytic normalisation: L(s,F) = prod_p (1 - a_p p^-s + conj(a_p) p^-2s - p^-3s)^-1 (FKLR eq. (1.3) p.2; FKL p.13: a_{p^2} = a_p^2 - conj(a_p)); a_p = alpha1+alpha2+alpha3, alpha1 alpha2 alpha3 = 1, |alpha_i| = 1 is the (unproved) Ramanujan conjecture, not imposed in the FKLR search. A(1,p) = conj(A(p,1)).
gamma_factor: Lambda(s,F) = Gamma_R(s + i*lambda1) Gamma_R(s + i*lambda2) Gamma_R(s - i*(lambda1+lambda2)) L(s,F), Gamma_R(s) = pi^(-s/2) Gamma(s/2); Lambda(s,F) = conj(Lambda(1 - conj(s), F)) = Lambda(1 - s, dual F); N = 1, epsilon = 1 (FKL eq. (3.2) p.3 with N=1, eps=1, d1=3 stated on p.4; FKLR eqs. (2.3)-(2.5) p.3-4 and (3.1) p.7). Checked here numerically: every A_p1 below satisfies this functional equation (see checks).
functional_equation_in_AFE_form: Lambda(s) = Q^s prod_j Gamma(s/2 + i*lambda_j/2) L(s), Q = pi^(-3/2) (FKL eq. (4.2) p.10 and p.12). NB: FKL p.12 writes lambda = (8.4i, 14.2i, -22.6i) directly in Gamma(kappa s + lambda_j); the printed numbers of eq. (4.8) are reproduced only with Gamma(s/2 + 4.2i) etc., i.e. Gamma_R(s + 8.4i), so the example is (lambda1, lambda2) = (8.4, 14.2) in the convention above (own computation). The GitHub file stores x = lambda/2 and a template {-XX[1], XX[2], -XX[1]-XX[2]} or {XX[1], XX[2], -XX[1]-XX[2]}; the literal minus template fails the FE by 1e5-1e9.

rankin_selberg.gamma_factor: Lambda(s, F x F~) = Gamma_R(s)^3 * prod over d in {lambda1-lambda2, 2*lambda1+lambda2, lambda1+2*lambda2} of Gamma_R(s+i d) Gamma_R(s-i d) * L(s, F x F~) = [Gamma_R(s) zeta(s)] * [Gamma_R(s)^2 prod_d Gamma_R(s+id)Gamma_R(s-id) L(s, Ad F)]; local factor at p: prod_{j,k} (1 - alpha_j conj(alpha_k) p^-s)^-1.
rankin_selberg.poles: Lambda(s, F x F~) has simple poles at s = 0 and s = 1 (classical Jacquet-Piatetski-Shapiro-Shalika / Jacquet-Shalika; NOT stated in FKL or FKLR; source not read in this run).
rankin_selberg.positivity_form: Miller, Duke Math. J. 112 (2002), arXiv math/0112196v1, Sec. 8 eq. (13) p.32: int g(x)(e^{x/2}+e^{-x/2}) dx + 2 Re sum_{j,k} l(mu_jk) + g(0) log D >= 0, mu_jk = archimedean Gamma_R parameters of pi x pi~ (here i(lambda_j - lambda_k)), coefficients dropped because -L'/L has non-negative coefficients; l(eta) = (1/2pi) int h(r) Gamma_R'/Gamma_R(1/2 + eta + i r) dr (eq. (3) p.5-6).
rankin_selberg.derived_here: The Gamma factor list is derived here from mu_j = i lambda_j (algebra, not printed in FKL/FKLR); the three differences are exactly those in the FKLR Plancherel density p.18.

miller_region.statement_read: Miller, Duke 2002 (arXiv math/0112196v1) Sec. 6.1 Criteria p.26: if sum_j s(r_j) < 0 then there is no cuspidal eigenfunction on SL_n(Z)\SL_n(R)/SO_n(R) with Im mu_j = r_j; s(r) = max over sigma in [-1/2, 3/2] of Re l_{1,1/2}(i r + sigma), test function g_{1,p} supported in [-p, p], p = 1/2 (no primes enter). Prop. 6.1 p.26: s(r) < 0 for |r| < 7.2, so sum r_j^2 > 51.84 (1 + 1/(n-1)) (= 77.76 for n = 3). Thm 6.3 p.27 with d = 174 (p.29): Laplace eigenvalue >= 87.625 for n = 3, i.e. for tempered forms sum r_j^2 = 2(l1^2+l1 l2+l2^2) >= 174, l1^2+l1 l2+l2^2 >= 87.
miller_region.fkl_statement: FKL p.4: "Miller also proved the Selberg eigenvalue conjecture for SL(3,Z) in the form lambda1^2+lambda1 lambda2+lambda2^2 >= 80. (Miller proved slightly more, which is described in Figure 3.1)"; Fig. 3.1 p.5: darkest region = Miller's excluded region [Mil1 = Crelle 533 (2001)] via the explicit formula. The arXiv v1 of that Crelle paper (math/0006058) has no such region (Weyl law, temperedness a.e., lambda >= 1 only); the published version was not read.
miller_region.figure_boundary_digitized: Own digitisation of FKL Fig. 3.1 (gl3eigs.png in the arXiv source), axes calibrated on the 124 plotted forms (122 matched, rms 0.6 px = 0.05 units; frame = [0,24]x[0,20]). Black (Miller) region along rays at angle theta from the lambda1-axis ends at r = 9.30 (5 deg), 9.24 (10), 9.34 (15), 9.60 (20), 10.14 (25), 10.90 (30), 12.56 (35), 16.52 (40), 23.7 (44), 24.4 (45, spike tip near lambda1 = lambda2 = 17.2); symmetric about the diagonal. Near the axes this is l1^2+l1 l2+l2^2 ~ 94-109, i.e. a little outside the disk value 87. The diagonal spike cannot come from the Sec. 6 criterion (s(r) > 0 for |r| > 7.2); its source is not identified in what was read (a Rankin-Selberg argument would favour the diagonal: heuristic).
miller_region.fkl_theorem_3_1: FKL Thm 3.1 p.4 (proof Sec. 7 p.17-18): assuming |a_p| <= 3, no L-function with d=3, N=1 in the lighter (purple) region of Fig. 3.1; method: AFE with several test functions + Ramanujan bound (3.4) on all other coefficients; example (8.4, 14.2): b2(2) < -3.8842 contradicts |a_2| <= 3.
miller_region.first_forms_vs_boundary: No remark in FKL or FKLR that the first forms lie close to the excluded boundary (both read in full). Digitised: the first five forms by Laplace eigenvalue lie 0.13, 0.52, 0.13, 0.52, 0.42 lambda-units from the nearest purple (FKL Thm 3.1) pixel (dot radius ~0.15), and 1.4-4.1 units from the black region; FKL p.7 remark: some of the first L-functions lie approximately along certain lines (Fig. 3.1 and 3.2); FKLR p.8: striations along slopes 0 and 1.

first_form.fklr: FKLR Fig. 4.1 p.13 uses (lambda1, lambda2) ~ (14.141, 2.380) as its r0r0r0 example; a commented-out source line (not printed) calls it "among the very first".
first_form.completeness_claim: FKL p.4: the 124 lowest (lexicographic) found; "we believe that the figure shows all cases with lambda1 <= 20, and may include all with lambda1 <= 24". FKLR p.11: almost all found through the first few Plancherel contours, much smaller percentage further out.

zeta_zero_remark: None found. FKL and FKLR (read in full) do not relate spectral parameters to zeros of zeta. The only zeta-zero remark is FKL p.7-8 (and Bober et al.): the first Sp(4,Z) L-function has its first zero at 14.496 > 14.1347. Own arithmetic: 14.14163558 - 14.13472514 = 0.0069; with about 50 forms per unit of lambda1 near 14-34 such a near-coincidence is not unusual (heuristic).
data_caveats: The GitHub file stores, for 242 of 1050 entries, the coefficients of the dual form (conj a_p) relative to the stated Gamma factor; they are conjugated here. Decided by the FE test; 6 self-dual (lambda2 ~ 0) entries pass both ways.

Accuracy of a_p falls along each list: for the 6 self-dual entries |Im a_p| (should be 0) is <= 2e-11 for p <= 13, <= 2e-8 at p = 17, <= 6e-7 at p = 19, 7e-11..1e-4 at p = 23, 7e-7..0.3 for p >= 29. 67 entries have some listed a_p outside the SU(3) deltoid (|a_p| up to 14), all at p >= 31 (62 of them at p = 37); none at p <= 29.
Entry with lambda = (27.55934452, 11.354064152) has an unresolved symbol in a_17 (omitted).

The source gives no per-number accuracy (GitHub README: "a better version of the data, indicating the accuracy of each number, is being prepared"). FKL Table 3.1: "truncated to 8 correct decimals". fe_residual below is our own consistency measure (median 5e-10, 90% < 3e-6, max 2.5e-2).
Only the spherical type r0r0r0 is listed. The same repository has 1525408-byte r0r1r1 (sign -1) and 5717067-byte r-delta-c2kappa files for the other degree-3 conductor-1 Gamma types (not parsed).

(p.17-18) reproduced (last digit differs by truncation); the printed rigorous ranges +-1.33, +-0.301 are not reproduced (own d_3(n) bound gives +-1.03, +-0.27; FKL do not state their bound sum)
checks.fkl_table_3_1: lambda, a2, a3 of all 15 rows agree with the FE-oriented GitHub data to < 1e-8 (max 9.7e-9; table truncated to 8 decimals)
checks.lmfdb: 101 LMFDB degree-3 conductor-1 records (API, 26 Nov 2026) matched: a_2 agrees with the FE-oriented data in 101/101 (LMFDB stores both F and dual F, mu_imag negated and a_p conjugated); LMFDB labels = rounded (2 decimals) |mu| sorted, p/m sign, 101/101
checks.fe_test: for each entry Z(1/2+i) computed with g(s) = exp(-i beta s), beta in {0, 1/4, 1/2}, a_n from a_p by the Hecke recursion, unknown a_n bounded by d_3(n); orientation decided when one choice has spread < 0.1 and the other is > 1e4 times larger
